title: Map of Highest Peak
summary: Given an integer matrix isWater of size m x n, where each cell is either a land cell (indicated by 0) or a water cell (indicated by 1), assign a non-negative height to each cell such that: - Water cells must have a height of 0.
statement: Given an integer matrix isWater of size m x n, where each cell is either a land cell (indicated by 0) or a water cell (indicated by 1), assign a non-negative height to each cell such that: - Water cells must have a height of 0. - The height difference between any two adjacent cells must be at most 1. Cells are considered adjacent if they are directly north, east, south, or west of each other. Your task is to find an assignment of heights that maximizes the maximum height in the matrix. Return an integer matrix height of size m x n, where height[i][j] represents the height of cell (i, j). If multiple solutions exist, any valid solution is acceptable.
constraints: Water cells contain one and must receive height zero; land cells contain zero.
Assign nonnegative heights with adjacent differences at most one, maximizing the highest height; return the height matrix.
hints: The greatest valid height at a cell is its shortest Manhattan path distance to water.
Run breadth-first search simultaneously from every water cell at height zero.
Assign each unseen neighbor current+1 and enqueue it.
Distance-to-nearest-water satisfies every edge bound, and no valid assignment can exceed path length along a route to water.
editorial: Distance-to-nearest-water satisfies every edge bound, and no valid assignment can exceed path length along a route to water.
